findings.title: Frame event ID and payload separately in Merkle commitments
findings.evidence: new() hashes event_id.as_bytes(), then payload, then parent_hash without lengths or separators; constructor accepts arbitrary String IDs.
findings.trigger: Construct nodes with the same parent and (event_id="a",payload=b"bc") versus (event_id="ab",payload=b"c").
findings.impact: Both distinct nodes receive the same state_hash without breaking SHA-256. The exported constructor does not bind field boundaries; current in-file tests use fixed-form IDs only.

findings.title: Escape user-controlled values before producing YAML
findings.evidence: Topic and decision strings are interpolated directly into double-quoted YAML scalars (lines 41-44,50).
findings.trigger: run_grill_you(topic=...) receives a topic containing a quote, backslash or newline.
findings.impact: to_yaml() can return invalid YAML or injected YAML fields rather than faithfully serializing the supplied topic. No downstream privileged YAML consumer was established.

findings.title: Retain incomplete transcript records until the next append
findings.evidence: readlines() consumes an unterminated trailing record, last_pos=f.tell() advances past it, and extract_model_change silently drops JSON decode failures.
findings.trigger: A writer appends a JSON record in two writes straddling a watcher polling interval.
findings.impact: The first fragment is discarded and the remaining fragment cannot reconstruct the record, permanently losing the model-change announcement.

findings.title: Reset tail position when transcript is truncated or replaced
findings.evidence: Only curr_size > last_pos is handled; last_pos is never reset and no file identity is tracked.
findings.trigger: The watched transcript is truncated/rotated and the replacement starts shorter than the prior offset.
findings.impact: Announcements stop until the new file exceeds the old size and then resume from an arbitrary offset, losing earlier replacement-file events.

findings.title: Pass notification text as data rather than AppleScript source
findings.evidence: The cached-audio branch interpolates text directly into osascript -e source inside a quoted string; subprocess receives this source unchanged.
findings.trigger: speak_cloned receives quote-bearing text and the corresponding cached/direct WAV exists (lines 51-58).
findings.impact: Text can terminate the AppleScript string, corrupt the notification or introduce AppleScript expressions under the announcer account. The cache-hit precondition limits reachability; no remote trust boundary is asserted.

findings.title: Limit terminology rewrites to comments and documentation
findings.evidence: For any MythologicalTerm issue the fixer applies every replacement regex to the entire file, including executable identifiers, protocol strings and literals.
findings.trigger: A flagged source file contains an identifier or protocol value named oracle or magic referenced elsewhere.
findings.impact: Running the fixer changes code behavior or breaks cross-file references without updating consumers; terminology cleanup is not semantics preserving.

findings.title: Remove comments from multipart JSON metadata example
findings.evidence: The curl metadata form contains "compatibility_date": "2026-01-01" followed by a // comment inside the JSON field.
findings.trigger: Copy the Deploy with Bindings metadata example into an actual request after replacing the abbreviated URL.
findings.impact: The metadata payload is invalid JSON, so the example cannot deploy the requested bindings. This is a static example defect, not an observed service failure.

findings.title: Avoid redeclaring the imported DispatchNamespace name
findings.evidence: One TypeScript block imports type DispatchNamespace and then declares interface DispatchNamespace in the same module (lines 36-40).
findings.trigger: Use the TypeScript Types block as written in a TypeScript module.
findings.impact: The imported type name conflicts with the local declaration, making the reference example fail type checking.

findings.title: Do not claim strict real-time determinism from one benchmark maximum
findings.evidence: The only displayed evidence is one pair of aggregate benchmark results, yet lines 46-50 claim mathematical proof, strict real-time determinism, and patentability.
findings.trigger: A reader relies on this audit as evidence of a worst-case timing guarantee or established patentability.
findings.impact: A finite observed maximum does not establish a worst-case bound, nor do these results establish patentability. The document overstates the evidence and should qualify these conclusions.

hypotheses.hypothesis: stepAgent can emit CommitAction from Idle without stepSession or a Z3 witness; the session no-bypass theorem concerns only stepSession. This is a mismatch between the modeled APIs, not evidence of an executable authorization bypass. A runtime consumer/refinement path was not traced.

ScittL5Receipt is described as COSE Sign1 but seal() computes only an unkeyed hash. No signing or verifier consumer was established in the scoped source reads; investigate whether callers treat this exported structure as authenticated attestation.

tool_limitations: No native codebase-memory graph tools were exposed: discovery of ALL_TOOLS for search_graph/get_architecture returned none; targeted text search used.
Audit-only: no repository tests, builds, runtime, service/API calls or formal compilation executed. Historical evidence JSON was reviewed as source material, not revalidated runtime evidence.
External SDK/API claims were not validated against current official documentation; findings in reference files are limited to language/serialization defects.
